rules.statement: A notarial lease is a pro tanto alienation, and gives the lessee during his term the legal remedies of an owner and possessor.
rules.supporting_quote: "It appears that, according to the Roman Law, where a land or house was let, the 'conductor,' who in the case of hind was termed colonus, and in the case of a house inquilinus, was not regarded as possessing the demised premises, for he did not claim to hold them ut dominus, which was of the essence of possession, so that the lessor was still the possessor, notwithstanding the letting. If, therefore, the tenant were ejected by a third person, he was not entitled to the action rei vindicatio, nor to the ordinary possessory interdicts. But by the Roman-Dutch Law, where a lease was for a substantial period, the tenant had the right to sue his lessor to compel him to give up the use of the premises during the term, and was not restricted to an action for damages for breach of contract."
